edition.notes: A dated delivery state of a transcription of Migne, not a critical edition. The file was checked for the automated Italian spelling corruption that affects some other files on the same site and was clean. Consumers needing a critical text must use the relevant Corpus Christianorum edition, which was not consulted. The transcription embeds Migne's column numbers in the form (0625B), which is how columns are cited from it. No page image of Patrologia Latina 92 at these columns was reachable: the Internet Archive scan of that volume that was located contains only the Matthew and Mark commentaries.

passages.context: Bede's complete exposition of Luke 10:23-37 in Book III, read in the retrieved file at the embedded Migne column markers 0467C through 0470D. Registered for three findings used by the Twelfth Sunday after Pentecost proper guide: his treatment of the blessed eyes (the eyes of the little ones to whom the Son deigns to reveal himself and the Father, against the scribes who saw only the Lord's body; the prophets and kings who saw per speculum et in aenigmate); his rule that the parable teaches everyone who shows mercy to be a neighbour AND specially designates the Son of God, so that allegory must not thin out or remove the moral institutes of mutual brotherhood (ut omnem qui misericordiam faceret cuilibet proximum doceret ... neque enim ... moralia mutuae fraternitatis instituta sub allegoriae regulis extenuare et auferre conemur); and his allegorical table, taken largely verbatim from Augustine's Quaestiones Evangeliorum II.19 and Ambrose's Expositio in Lucam VII, with his own extensions (the denarii given altera die because the risen Lord opened the Scriptures; the innkeeper widened from Paul to the Spirit-taught preachers).
passages.notes: The whole retrieved wikitext was re-fetched on 2026-08-19 and its SHA-256 matched this artifact record before reading. The work record's locus grammar admits only a single verse token, so the locus names the pericope's opening verse; the passage inspected and verified is Bede's whole exposition of Luke 10:23-37, at physical lines 1034-1068 of that file. The line placement is recorded here as prose because the artifact's bytes are registered remote rather than retained, so no replayable physical-line locator is claimed.

passages.context: Bede's harmonizing note on Luke 24:12, read in the retrieved file at the embedded Migne column markers 0625A and 0625B, with the preceding remark on the disciples' slowness to believe and the following note on Emmaus in view. Registered as the earliest witness located that notices the Luke and John difference at this point and works at it, and as a material negative: Bede reconciles the seeing and says nothing of the believing or of theft.
passages.notes: The transcription's parenthetical reference (Luc. XXIV) and the column marker (0625B), both of which fall inside this passage in the delivered file, are apparatus of the transcription and of Migne and are omitted. work.author: Bede the Venerable
work.description: Bede's commentary on Luke in six books, completed about 715 and dedicated to Acca of Hexham. Book VI covers the passion and resurrection narratives, including a harmonizing note on Luke 24:12 that reconciles Luke's and John's accounts of who looked into the tomb. Edition records keep Migne's Latin, dated web deliveries of it, and modern translations apart; the modern English translation is under copyright and is not registered here.
work.title: In Lucae evangelium expositio
